newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank trading volume surges in May.
newsitem.headline: China interbank trading volume surges in May.

text.p: Trading volume on the Shanghai interbank money market hit 59.889 billion yuan ($7.22 billion) in May, with daily volume averaging 2.852 billion yuan, a surge of 42.73 percent from April, the Securities Times said on Thursday.
The head offices of major state banks traded actively in May, with money borrowed and lent rocketing 171.29 percent and 67.72 percent respectively, the newspaper said.
Traders on the market include Chinese and foreign banks, short-term financial centres -- money brokerages run by the central bank -- securities houses and insurance companies.
Daily trading volume fluctuated at the beginning of May and gradually stabilised later in the month, the newspaper said.
The market's daily trading volume monthly high of 5.837 billion yuan and and low of 1.597 billion yuan both came early in May, the newspaper said.
The weighted average interbank rates of all seven contracts, ranging from one-day to 120-day, fell last month with short-term contracts trading more actively than long-term contracts, it said.
